label: Wayfair (supplier)
terms_note: Wayfair supplier approval (Partner Home); the supplier registers an application under Developer › Applications; OAuth2 client credentials; sandbox host; rate limits enforced (numbers not on the page); commercial terms are Wayfair's supplier / dropship agreement (Wayfair sets retail prices).

discovery.auth: oauth2 client credentials (client id/secret from Partner Home › Developer › Applications; token from sso.auth.wayfair.com)

rate_limits: open-PO query at most every 3 s (≤25 POs per call, poll every 30 min); accept/ASN 1 request per 3 s; inventory TRUE_UP at least daily, DIFFERENTIAL ideally every 30 min

auth: 1. Supplier approved by Wayfair; Partner Home › Developer › Applications → client id + secret (sandbox and production apps).
2. POST client_credentials to sso.auth.wayfair.com → bearer token.
3. GraphQL queries / mutations against the API host.
reference.limits: Enforced; thresholds not on the page read. - Supplier / dropship agreement; Wayfair is the retailer of record and sets prices. - Partner Home application per supplier.
mcp_sdk: none official found in the pages opened

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: Production Client ID of your application (Wayfair Developer Portal > Application Management; needs the 'API' role in Partner Home and a completed sandbox test).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: Production Client Secret of the same application; exchanged at https://sso.auth.wayfair.com/oauth/token for a 24-hour bearer token.

config_fields.name: supplier_id
config_fields.help: Numeric Wayfair supplier ID used in inventory feeds: your warehouse ID for a child-level feed, or the supplier account ID for a parent-level feed (Partner Home > Warehouse Management).

adapter.terms: Wayfair supplier GraphQL API (POST https://api.wayfair.com/v1/graphql) for suppliers already selling on Wayfair with Partner Home access; production permissions are granted after sandbox testing. GraphQL failures come back as {errors: [...]} in a 200 body.

body.query: =query getDropshipPurchaseOrders($limit: Int32) { getDropshipPurchaseOrders(limit: $limit) { poNumber poDate supplierId } }

me.note: There is no account query; the probe mints a token and runs getDropshipPurchaseOrders(limit: 1).

body.query: =query getDropshipPurchaseOrders($limit: Int32, $hasResponse: Boolean, $fromDate: IsoDateTime, $sortOrder: SortOrder) { getDropshipPurchaseOrders(limit: $limit, hasResponse: $hasResponse, fromDate: $fromDate, sortOrder: $sortOrder) { poNumber poDate supplierId products { partNumber quantity price } } }

list_orders.note: getDropshipPurchaseOrders(limit ≤ 25, default 10; hasResponse; fromDate; sortOrder ASC by poDate) for drop-ship POs. status: `open` = POs you have not responded to (hasResponse false), `accepted` = POs already answered; omit for both. since = fromDate (ISO date-time, UTC). There are no pages: advance `since` to the last poDate. Rows carry poNumber, poDate, supplierId and products {partNumber, quantity, price} (in raw).

body.query: =mutation saveInventory($inventory: [inventoryInput]!, $feedKind: inventoryFeedKind) { inventory { save(inventory: $inventory, feedKind: $feedKind) { handle status itemCount errorCount errors { key message } } } }

set_inventory.note: inventory.save mutation with feedKind DIFFERENTIAL (a partial feed; production only) and one line {supplierId (config), supplierPartNumber = sku, quantityOnHand = quantity}. `sku` is required; `listing_id` is ignored. Processing is asynchronous: status starts as PROCESSING; per-item validation errors are in raw errors. The daily TRUE_UP full feed is not sent by this tool.

body.query: =mutation saveInventory($inventory: [inventoryInput]!, $feedKind: inventoryFeedKind) { inventory { save(inventory: $inventory, feedKind: $feedKind) { handle status itemCount errorCount errors { key message } } } }

end_listing.note: Discontinues a part: inventory.save with {supplierId, supplierPartNumber = listing_id, quantityOnHand 0, discontinued: true} (DIFFERENTIAL). 'To discontinue an item, send discontinued: true once'; it can be reversed within about 90 days. With a child-level feed every warehouse must be discontinued.

not_offered.create_listing: Product Addition is an asynchronous orchestrated workflow: discover taxonomyCategoryId and its attribute questions, a manufacturerId from brandAssociations and a marketContext, then submit and poll submissions (https://developer.wayfair.io/posts/catalog-product-addition); the vocabulary has no category, brand or attributes.
not_offered.update_listing: Product Update is asynchronous and split by level: updateMarketSpecificCatalogItems needs a marketContext (country, brand, language, locale) and item-group updates the SKU itemGroupId, with results polled through statusOfUpdateRequest (https://developer.wayfair.io/posts/catalog-product-update); prices are not part of it.
not_offered.mark_shipped: The shipment (ASN) mutation requires supplierId, packageCount, carrierCode (SCAC), shipSpeed, shipDate, sourceAddress and per-package items {partNumber, quantity} matching the PO (https://developer.wayfair.io/posts/dropship-orders-asn); the vocabulary only carries order_id, carrier and tracking_number.

evidence: host api.wayfair.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)
probe: 4/4 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 4/4 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; names not found on the page: end_listing:query, set_inventory:query
